newsitem.title: CHINA: China dissident politician in family's custody.
newsitem.headline: China dissident politician in family's custody.

text.p: Bao Tong, the most senior Chinese official jailed after the 1989 student protests for democracy, has been released into the custody of his family after nearly a year under house arrest, relatives said on Wednesday.
"But it remains to be seen how much freedom (he) will have in future," his son, Bao Puliu, said by telephone from the United States.

Bao Tong, former aide to disgraced Communist Party chief Zhao Ziyang, was released in May 1996 after serving seven years in prison for his role in the 1989 demonstrations and immediately placed under house arrest in a house in the suburbs of Beijing.
He and his family moved into a new, third-floor flat in Shijingshan in western Beijing last Saturday after the family agreed to move from their government residence.
"Bao Tong is being shunted to Shijingshan to make it easier to control him," said a source close to the family who asked not to be identified.

Diplomats say Bao is a source of anxiety for China's leaders, who fear he may reveal details of the dealings of the highest party and government echelons in the weeks before the bloody June 4, 1989, crackdown on demonstrators.
